Text.Text: Ledger's closed, final page signed. The annex is a school again instead of a wound, and the guard you carry out of it never broke once. That's the only grade that matters now. Hold it where nobody's keeping score.
Your grip'll do. Your recovery won't. Get your Vibroblade training to rank 50, then report back. I'm sending a fighter into the annex, not a name for the casualty list.

Six Invincible adepts have taken the militia annex here in Veles. I taught them to stay on their feet, and they've decided that makes everyone else expendable. Put the six down and bring me their drill ledger. I want to know who they're answering to.
Here's the annex key. The entrance is in the Veles Sheriff and Clinic. Check your grip before you use it. Then bring me that ledger.

A guard that does not break. Not bravado, not thick armor, not planting your boots because pride won't let you move. A line you hold with a vibroblade until shot, blade, and bad luck have all given up on it. Most who claim the form are lying. The drill floor sorts those out.

My former students sealed it after deciding the drills no longer needed my approval. The entrance is here in the Sheriff and Clinic. My key will get you through; making them listen will take more work.

Mine. Every adept on that floor either washed out of my program or refused to leave it, and they've drilled my forms every day since, angry. The last curious visitor who wandered in spent a month over a med table. They won't break formation because you ask nicely. Make them.
Six adepts in the Veles Militia Annex. Bring their drill ledger back to the Sheriff and Clinic. Feet under you, eyes up.
That shape in your pack had better be my drill ledger. On the table.
Present and intact. Blood on the corner, not yours, by the way you're standing. First rotation: pass. Take the pay, eat something, sleep. The next line on this ledger is not this polite.

Five specialists are running the annex range off a relay that used to be mine. Get the five out of my firing lanes and bring the relay back. A drill stops when someone calls it. They've forgotten that part.
Back to the annex. Keep your elbow in when you press them. Quick hands still need a good recovery.

Specialists earned rank under me before the shutdown. The pass bar was holding a guard through a full rotation without one scored hit, and all five cleared it. You'll be the first live drill they've had in a year. They have been bored. Bored and good is a bad combination for you.

The relay logs every run on that range: names, times, scores. It's their proof the program still functions without a captain. On my desk it becomes proof of the opposite. Command ignores rumors and respects records, so I collect records.

Open lanes, no cover worth the word, and five blades timing exactly how long your guard holds, because timing guards is what that range is for. Keep your feet moving between lanes and make them re-aim. The range rewards patience. It buries heroes.
The five specialists in the annex have the range relay. Beat them and get it back here.
You're standing straighter than last week. Range time does that. The relay, on the desk.

Relay checks out. Last run it ever logged is yours, which is a kind of score I can live with. Second rotation: pass. You're no stranger to the annex now, which means the annex knows you're coming. Watch the shadows past the range.

The warden holds the annex. Challenge him there, beat him, and bring me the scored badge he wears. Find yourself some backup. I know what he can take, and I know what he'll do while you're finding out.
Call Sarn at the annex challenge marker. When he squares up, keep your guard honest. Let your partners help if you've brought them; don't make this a contest in taking hits. Bring the badge home.

Sarn. Six years my second. When command pulled the program he stayed inside the gate and I obeyed the order out of it, and neither of us has forgiven the other. He runs that gate exactly the way I taught him: nothing passes that hasn't earned it. He won't pull the blow. Don't pull yours.

Scored challenge badges went to trainees who survived a full challenge rotation against me, personally. Sarn's is the only one etched with a perfect score. While he wears it, he outranks every drill in the annex. When it sits on my desk, the rank comes back where it belongs.

Corporal Dessa Vane. Fast feet, good guard, no patience. She took the inner gate alone against my written order. Sarn's first exchange broke her arm through the block, and the second she never saw. I signed for the body. I'm not signing for another one, so you go with company or you don't go.
Call the warden at the annex challenge marker. Beat him and bring back the challenge badge.
You're walking in without a limp. Either you never fought him, or you learned faster than Vane did. The badge. Show me.

His badge. Blood on the pin and a perfect score under it. He'd have fought you seriously, which means you passed something I can't teach from this side of the gate. Third rotation: pass, distinguished. Buy your partners a round. Log it as equipment maintenance.
Four officers still have the captain's chit. They're signing off on the drills that keep this school alive. Defeat the four in the annex and bring it to me. I'll put an end to the orders.
Recover the chit. Don't lose your footing just because they know their captain's watching.

Toma, Verik, Onn, and Pale. Ten years of my mornings went into those four, and they earned every stripe I gave them before they chose the annex over the stand-down order. I'm not neutral about this line and I won't pretend otherwise. Grade them honestly. Beat what I built without insulting it.

A captain's challenge chit. Whoever holds it can demand a graded bout with the captain, any hour, any floor. I surrendered mine the day they sealed the gate, and the circle keeps it as proof the annex still answers to a captain. It does. The wrong one.

You don't beat four overlapping guards with one blade, so don't audition for it. Bring the partners from the gate fight. Drag one guard out of the line, hit the seam he leaves, and reset before the plates close. A circle only breaks from inside a gap. Your job is the gap.
Four officers in the annex still have the captain's chit. Put them down and bring it here.
Four at once. I drilled that formation for ten years and never once saw it opened. The chit, trainee. Last time I get to call you that.
My chit. Lighter than I remembered. Fourth rotation: pass, full marks, and I'm done pretending you're a trainee. One line left in this ledger. In twenty years I have never had cause to mark it.
The master is in the Militia Command Room. Call her at its challenge marker and beat her. She'll want you trying to prove you can take another hit. Don't indulge her. Come back here when she's down.

Logged, final line. Center floor, past where the circle stood. Partners on your flanks, patience in the first minute, no heroics. And whatever she says to you in there, she's earned the right to say it.

Finished means no seams. The circle overlapped four guards; Serra is one guard with no gap in it. Blade, shot, flank, feint, she has already turned it before you commit. You will land nothing in your first minute, so spend it learning her tempo while your partners keep her turning. Even a perfect guard faces one direction at a time. That's the entire lesson, if you live to use it.

She stayed because she believed the program was right and command was wrong, and I sealed the gate on her because an order is an order. We've both had years to chew on that. When her guard breaks, the annex stops being a wound and can be a school again. Maybe with her teaching in it. That page isn't written yet. Yours is first.

I took my challenge rotation against her the spring before the shutdown. Best day I ever had with a blade in my hand, and she graded it a fail and helped me off the floor. A captain gets one more failure than his pride can afford, then he stops spending his trainees' respect and sends someone better. Today, better is you.
The Militia Command Room has the master's challenge marker. Beat her and report back to the Sheriff and Clinic.
The annex went quiet an hour ago. I've stood posts outside that gate half my life and never once heard it quiet. Report, plainly: did her guard break?
She's down, and you're standing. Good. Take your pay. If you still want Invincible taught properly, report back after you've rested. We start with footwork, whether you like that answer or not.
About the assignment, Captain.
Sign me in, Captain.
What exactly is Invincible?
Why is the annex sealed?
Who's holding that drill floor?
Not yet, Captain.
Your drill ledger, Captain. Six adepts couldn't hold their line.
Back to the range assignment.
Consider them retired.
What makes these specialists dangerous?
Why does the relay matter?
What's the range like inside?
I need more drill time first.
One range relay, five specialists off the score sheet.
About the warden.
I'll bring the blades. Sign me in.
Who is Sarn to you?
What's the badge worth?
What happened to the last one who went alone?
Then I wait until I have my two.
Sarn's badge, Captain. Perfect score and all.
Back to the circle.
The circle breaks. You have my word.
Who are the four?
What is the chit?
How does a formation like that break?
Not until my people are ready.
No formation left standing. Your chit, Captain.
About Serra Kel.
Then let's close your ledger.
What am I facing in her guard?
Why did she stay behind the gate?
Why isn't this your fight, Captain?
Not yet. Not for this one.
It broke, Captain. The floor is yours again.
